Nodes communicate by\n// scheduling MessageEvents; user code can schedule FuncEvents (gossip ticks,\n// client writes, link partitions, link healing). Per-link behaviour —\n// latency, loss, duplication, reordering — is driven by a seeded RNG so a run\n// is fully reproducible from its JSON scenario.\npackage sim\n\nimport (\n\t\"container/heap\"\n\t\"math/rand\"\n\t\"sort\"\n)\n\n// Event is anything the clock can deliver.\ntype Event interface {\n\tAt() int64\n\tsetAt(int64)\n\tkindTag() string\n}\n\n// baseEvent carries heap bookkeeping.\ntype baseEvent struct {\n\tat int64\n\t// index lets heap.Fix/Remove work.\n\tindex int\n\t// seq ties equal timestamps apart deterministically (insertion order).\n\tseq uint64\n}\n\nfunc (e *baseEvent) At() int64      { return e.at }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) setAt(t int64)  { e.at = t }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) kindTag() string { return \"\" }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) seqVal() uint64 { return e.seq }\n\n// MessageEvent is a network message reaching dst.\ntype MessageEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tDst  string\n\tSize int64\n\t// Deliver hands the message to the destination node. It is an opaque\n\t// closure over the proto message so sim stays protocol-agnostic.\n\tDeliver func(now int64)\n\tTag     string\n}\n\nfunc (e *MessageEvent) kindTag() string { return \"msg:\" + e.Tag }\n\n// FuncEvent is a scheduled node/action callback.\ntype FuncEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tName string\n\tF    func(now int64)\n}\n\nfunc (e *FuncEvent) kindTag() string { return \"func:\" + e.Name }\n\n// eventHeap orders events by (time, sequence).\ntype eventHeap []Event\n\nfunc (h eventHeap) Len() int { return len(h) }\nfunc (h eventHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {\n\ta, b := h[i].At(), h[j].At()\n\tif a != b {\n\t\treturn a < b\n\t}\n\treturn h[i].(*baseEventProvider).seq() < h[j].(*baseEventProvider).seq()\n}\nfunc (h eventHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Push(x any)   { *h = append(*h, x.(Event)) }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Pop() any {\n\told := *h\n\tn := len(old)\n\tx := old[n-1]\n\t*h = old[:n-1]\n\treturn x\n}\n\n// baseEventProvider extracts the embedded baseEvent's tie-break sequence.\ntype baseEventProvider interface{ seq() uint64 }\n\nfunc (e *baseEvent) seq() uint64 { return e.seq }\n\n// LinkConfig describes one directed-ish link's fault profile. The same config\n// applies both ways (undirected edges), matching the partition model.\ntype LinkConfig struct {\n\tMinLatencyMS int64 `json:\"min_latency_ms\"`\n\tMaxLatencyMS int64 `json:\"max_latency_ms\"`\n\t// LossPct in [0,100]: probability a message copy is dropped.\n\tLossPct float64 `json:\"loss_pct\"`\n\t// DuplicatePct: probability an extra copy is scheduled.\n\tDuplicatePct float64 `json:\"duplicate_pct\"`\n\t// ReorderPct: probability a message is delayed one extra latency window,\n\t// which (combined with independent latencies) yields overtaking.\n\tReorderPct float64 `json:\"reorder_pct\"`\n}\n\n// LinkStats records traffic on one undirected link.\ntype LinkStats struct {\n\tSent      int64 `json:\"sent\"`\n\tDelivered int64 `json:\"delivered\"`\n\tLost      int64 `json:\"lost\"`\n\tDuplicated int64 `json:\"duplicated\"`\n\tBytesSent      int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesDelivered int64 `json:\"bytes_delivered\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the simulator's clock + links.\ntype Network struct {\n\trng       *rand.Rand\n\tevents    eventHeap\n\tnow       int64\n\tnextSeq   uint64\n\tlinks     map[string]LinkConfig\n\tdownUntil map[string]int64 // undirected pair -> down until this time (-1 forever)\n\tstats     map[string]*LinkStats\n\t// pending counts messages in flight, useful for convergence gating.\n\tpending int\n\n\t// MaxTimeMS bounds a run defensively (0 = unlimited).\n\tMaxTimeMS int64\n}\n\n// NewNetwork creates a simulator seeded deterministically.\nfunc NewNetwork(seed int64) *Network {\n\tn := &Network{\n\t\trng:       rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed)),\n\t\tlinks:     map[string]LinkConfig{},\n\t\tdownUntil: map[string]int64{},\n\t\tstats:     map[string]*LinkStats{},\n\t}\n\tn.events = eventHeap{}\n\theap.Init(&n.events)\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// SetLink registers an undirected link between a and b.\nfunc (n *Network) SetLink(a, b string, cfg LinkConfig) {\n\tn.links[pairKey(a, b)] = cfg\n}\n\n// Partition marks the link down until at least t (t <= 0 means forever).\nfunc (n *Network) Partition(a, b string, until int64) {\n\tn.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)] = until\n}\n\n// Heal brings the link back immediately.\nfunc (n *Network) Heal(a, b string) {\n\tdelete(n.downUntil, pairKey(a, b))\n}\n\n// IsDown reports the current link state.\nfunc (n *Network) IsDown(a, b string) bool {\n\tif t, ok := n.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)]; ok {\n\t\treturn t <= 0 || n.now < t\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Now returns the simulated time in ms.\nfunc (n *Network) Now() int64 { return n.now }\n\n// Pending reports messages currently queued for delivery.\nfunc (n *Network) Pending() int { return n.pending }\n\nfunc pairKey(a, b string) string {\n\tif a < b {\n\t\treturn a + \"\\x00\" + b\n\t}\n\treturn b + \"\\x00\" + a\n}\n\nfunc (n *Network) stat(a, b string) *LinkStats {\n\tk := pairKey(a, b)\n\ts := n.stats[k]\n\tif s == nil {\n\t\ts = &LinkStats{}\n\t\tn.stats[k] = s\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// Stats returns a snapshot of per-link counters (keys sorted for determinism).\nfunc (n *Network) Stats() map[string]LinkStats {\n\tout := make(map[string]LinkStats, len(n.stats))\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(n.stats))\n\tfor k, s := range n.stats {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t\tst := *s\n\t\tout[k] = st\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\t_ = keys\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// schedule inserts an event.\nfunc (n *Network) schedule(ev Event, at int64) {\n\tev.setAt(at)\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tif bp, ok := ev.(baseEventProvider); ok {\n\t\t// The concrete types embed baseEvent by value; store seq on it via a\n\t\t// tiny adapter to keep the heap tie-break stable.\n\t\t_ = bp\n\t}\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// ScheduleFunc runs f at simulated time t.\nfunc (n *Network) ScheduleFunc(name string, t int64, f func(now int64)) {\n\tev := &FuncEvent{Name: name, F: f}\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tev.baseEvent.seq = n.nextSeq\n\tev.setAt(t)\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// Send schedules the delivery of one message from src to dst according to the\n// link fault profile. size is the envelope's wire size for accounting.\nfunc (n *Network) Send(src, dst, tag string, size int64, deliver func(now int64)) {\n\tst := n.stat(src, dst)\n\tst.Sent++\n\tst.BytesSent += size\n\tn.pending++\n\n\tcfg := n.links[pairKey(src, dst)]\n\n\t// One \"original\" copy plus maybe a duplicate.\n\tn.scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag, size, deliver, cfg, st, false)\n\tif cfg.DuplicatePct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.DuplicatePct {\n\t\tst.Duplicated++\n\t\tn.scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag, size, deliver, cfg, st, true)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *Network) scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag string, size int64,\n\tdeliver func(now int64), cfg LinkConfig, st *LinkStats, dup bool) {\n\n\tif n.IsDown(src, dst) {\n\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif cfg.LossPct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.LossPct {\n\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tlat := cfg.MinLatencyMS\n\tif cfg.MaxLatencyMS > lat {\n\t\tlat += n.rng.Int63n(cfg.MaxLatencyMS - lat + 1)\n\t}\n\tif lat < 0 {\n\t\tlat = 0\n\t}\n\tif cfg.ReorderPct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.ReorderPct {\n\t\t// Push this copy late enough that later-sent messages can overtake it.\n\t\tlat += cfg.MaxLatencyMS + 1\n\t}\n\tat := n.now + lat\n\tev := &MessageEvent{Dst: dst, Size: size, Deliver: deliver, Tag: tag}\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tev.baseEvent.seq = n.nextSeq\n\t// A link may fail while the message is in flight: re-check at delivery.\n\toriginalSrc, originalDst := src, dst\n\tev.Deliver = func(now int64) {\n\t\tif n.IsDown(originalSrc, originalDst) {\n\t\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\t\tn.pending--\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tst.Delivered++\n\t\tst.BytesDelivered += size\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\tdeliver(now)\n\t}\n\tev.setAt(at)\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// Step advances one event. It returns false when no events remain (or the\n// defensive time bound is hit).\nfunc (n *Network) Step() bool {\n\tif n.events.Len() == 0 {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tev := heap.Pop(&n.events).(Event)\n\tif n.MaxTimeMS > 0 && ev.At() > n.MaxTimeMS {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tn.now = ev.At()\n\tswitch e := ev.(type) {\n\tcase *MessageEvent:\n\t\te.Deliver(n.now)\n\tcase *FuncEvent:\n\t\te.F(n.now)\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// RunUntilIdle processes all events.\nfunc (n *Network) RunUntilIdle() {\n\tfor n.Step() {\n\t}\n}\n\n// Run processes events while cont() Nodes communicate by\n// scheduling MessageEvents; user code can schedule FuncEvents (gossip ticks,\n// client writes, link partitions, link healing). Per-link behaviour —\n// latency, loss, duplication, reordering — is driven by a seeded RNG so a run\n// is fully reproducible from its JSON scenario.\npackage sim\n\nimport (\n\t\"container/heap\"\n\t\"math/rand\"\n\t\"sort\"\n)\n\n// Event is anything the clock can deliver.\ntype Event interface {\n\tAt() int64\n\tsetAt(int64)\n\tkindTag() string\n}\n\n// baseEvent carries heap bookkeeping.\ntype baseEvent struct {\n\tat int64\n\t// index lets heap.Fix/Remove work.\n\tindex int\n\t// seq ties equal timestamps apart deterministically (insertion order).\n\tseq uint64\n}\n\nfunc (e *baseEvent) At() int64      { return e.at }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) setAt(t int64)  { e.at = t }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) kindTag() string { return \"\" }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) seqVal() uint64 { return e.seq }\n\n// MessageEvent is a network message reaching dst.\ntype MessageEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tDst  string\n\tSize int64\n\t// Deliver hands the message to the destination node. It is an opaque\n\t// closure over the proto message so sim stays protocol-agnostic.\n\tDeliver func(now int64)\n\tTag     string\n}\n\nfunc (e *MessageEvent) kindTag() string { return \"msg:\" + e.Tag }\n\n// FuncEvent is a scheduled node/action callback.\ntype FuncEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tName string\n\tF    func(now int64)\n}\n\nfunc (e *FuncEvent) kindTag() string { return \"func:\" + e.Name }\n\n// eventHeap orders events by (time, insertion sequence).\ntype eventHeap []Event\n\nfunc (h eventHeap) Len() int { return len(h) }\nfunc (h eventHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {\n\ta, b := h[i].At(), h[j].At()\n\tif a != b {\n\t\treturn a < b\n\t}\n\treturn seqOf(h[i]) < seqOf(h[j])\n}\nfunc (h eventHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Push(x any)   { *h = append(*h, x.(Event)) }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Pop() any {\n\told := *h\n\tn := len(old)\n\tx := old[n-1]\n\t*h = old[:n-1]\n\treturn x\n}\n\n// seqProvider exposes the embedded baseEvent's tie-break sequence.\ntype seqProvider interface{ seqVal() uint64 }\n\nfunc seqOf(e Event) uint64 {\n\tif s, ok := e.(seqProvider); ok {\n\t\treturn s.seqVal()\n\t}\n\treturn 0\n}\n\n// LinkConfig describes one directed-ish link's fault profile. The same config\n// applies both ways (undirected edges), matching the partition model.\ntype LinkConfig struct {\n\tMinLatencyMS int64 `json:\"min_latency_ms\"`\n\tMaxLatencyMS int64 `json:\"max_latency_ms\"`\n\t// LossPct in [0,100]: probability a message copy is dropped.\n\tLossPct float64 `json:\"loss_pct\"`\n\t// DuplicatePct: probability an extra copy is scheduled.\n\tDuplicatePct float64 `json:\"duplicate_pct\"`\n\t// ReorderPct: probability a message is delayed one extra latency window,\n\t// which (combined with independent latencies) yields overtaking.\n\tReorderPct float64 `json:\"reorder_pct\"`\n}\n\n// LinkStats records traffic on one undirected link.\ntype LinkStats struct {\n\tSent      int64 `json:\"sent\"`\n\tDelivered int64 `json:\"delivered\"`\n\tLost      int64 `json:\"lost\"`\n\tDuplicated int64 `json:\"duplicated\"`\n\tBytesSent      int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesDelivered int64 `json:\"bytes_delivered\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the simulator's clock + links.\ntype Network struct {\n\trng       *rand.Rand\n\tevents    eventHeap\n\tnow       int64\n\tnextSeq   uint64\n\tlinks     map[string]LinkConfig\n\tdownUntil map[string]int64 // undirected pair -> down until this time (-1 forever)\n\tstats     map[string]*LinkStats\n\t// pending counts messages in flight, useful for convergence gating.\n\tpending int\n\n\t// MaxTimeMS bounds a run defensively (0 = unlimited).\n\tMaxTimeMS int64\n}\n\n// NewNetwork creates a simulator seeded deterministically.\nfunc NewNetwork(seed int64) *Network {\n\tn := &Network{\n\t\trng:       rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed)),\n\t\tlinks:     map[string]LinkConfig{},\n\t\tdownUntil: map[string]int64{},\n\t\tstats:     map[string]*LinkStats{},\n\t}\n\tn.events = eventHeap{}\n\theap.Init(&n.events)\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// SetLink registers an undirected link between a and b.\nfunc (n *Network) SetLink(a, b string, cfg LinkConfig) {\n\tn.links[pairKey(a, b)] = cfg\n}\n\n// Partition marks the link down until at least t (t <= 0 means forever).\nfunc (n *Network) Partition(a, b string, until int64) {\n\tn.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)] = until\n}\n\n// Heal brings the link back immediately.\nfunc (n *Network) Heal(a, b string) {\n\tdelete(n.downUntil, pairKey(a, b))\n}\n\n// IsDown reports the current link state.\nfunc (n *Network) IsDown(a, b string) bool {\n\tif t, ok := n.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)]; ok {\n\t\treturn t <= 0 || n.now < t\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Now returns the simulated time in ms.\nfunc (n *Network) Now() int64 { return n.now }\n\n// Pending reports messages currently queued for delivery.\nfunc (n *Network) Pending() int { return n.pending }\n\nfunc pairKey(a, b string) string {\n\tif a < b {\n\t\treturn a + \"\\x00\" + b\n\t}\n\treturn b + \"\\x00\" + a\n}\n\nfunc (n *Network) stat(a, b string) *LinkStats {\n\tk := pairKey(a, b)\n\ts := n.stats[k]\n\tif s == nil {\n\t\ts = &LinkStats{}\n\t\tn.stats[k] = s\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// Stats returns a snapshot of per-link counters (keys sorted for determinism).\nfunc (n *Network) Stats() map[string]LinkStats {\n\tout := make(map[string]LinkStats, len(n.stats))\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(n.stats))\n\tfor k, s := range n.stats {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t\tst := *s\n\t\tout[k] = st\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\t_ = keys\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// schedule inserts an event.\nfunc (n *Network) schedule(ev Event, at int64) {\n\tev.setAt(at)\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tif bp, ok := ev.(baseEventProvider); ok {\n\t\t// The concrete types embed baseEvent by value; store seq on it via a\n\t\t// tiny adapter to keep the heap tie-break stable.\n\t\t_ = bp\n\t}\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// ScheduleFunc runs f at simulated time t.\nfunc (n *Network) ScheduleFunc(name string, t int64, f func(now int64)) {\n\tev := &FuncEvent{Name: name, F: f}\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tev.baseEvent.seq = n.nextSeq\n\tev.setAt(t)\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// Send schedules the delivery of one message from src to dst according to the\n// link fault profile. size is the envelope's wire size for accounting.\nfunc (n *Network) Send(src, dst, tag string, size int64, deliver func(now int64)) {\n\tst := n.stat(src, dst)\n\tst.Sent++\n\tst.BytesSent += size\n\tn.pending++\n\n\tcfg := n.links[pairKey(src, dst)]\n\n\t// One \"original\" copy plus maybe a duplicate.\n\tn.scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag, size, deliver, cfg, st, false)\n\tif cfg.DuplicatePct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.DuplicatePct {\n\t\tst.Duplicated++\n\t\tn.scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag, size, deliver, cfg, st, true)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *Network) scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag string, size int64,\n\tdeliver func(now int64), cfg LinkConfig, st *LinkStats, dup bool) {\n\n\tif n.IsDown(src, dst) {\n\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif cfg.LossPct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.LossPct {\n\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tlat := cfg.MinLatencyMS\n\tif cfg.MaxLatencyMS > lat {\n\t\tlat += n.rng.Int63n(cfg.MaxLatencyMS - lat + 1)\n\t}\n\tif lat < 0 {\n\t\tlat = 0\n\t}\n\tif cfg.ReorderPct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.ReorderPct {\n\t\t// Push this copy late enough that later-sent messages can overtake it.\n\t\tlat += cfg.MaxLatencyMS + 1\n\t}\n\tat := n.now + lat\n\tev := &MessageEvent{Dst: dst, Size: size, Deliver: deliver, Tag: tag}\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tev.baseEvent.seq = n.nextSeq\n\t// A link may fail while the message is in flight: re-check at delivery.\n\toriginalSrc, originalDst := src, dst\n\tev.Deliver = func(now int64) {\n\t\tif n.IsDown(originalSrc, originalDst) {\n\t\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\t\tn.pending--\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tst.Delivered++\n\t\tst.BytesDelivered += size\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\tdeliver(now)\n\t}\n\tev.setAt(at)\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// Step advances one event. It returns false when no events remain (or the\n// defensive time bound is hit).\nfunc (n *Network) Step() bool {\n\tif n.events.Len() == 0 {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tev := heap.Pop(&n.events).(Event)\n\tif n.MaxTimeMS > 0 && ev.At() > n.MaxTimeMS {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tn.now = ev.At()\n\tswitch e := ev.(type) {\n\tcase *MessageEvent:\n\t\te.Deliver(n.now)\n\tcase *FuncEvent:\n\t\te.F(n.now)\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// RunUntilIdle processes all events.\nfunc (n *Network) RunUntilIdle() {\n\tfor n.Step() {\n\t}\n}\n\n// Run processes events while cont() returns true (or until idle).\nfunc (n *Network) Run(cont func(now int64) bool) {\n\tfor n.events.Len() > 0 {\n\t\tpeek := n.events[0].At()\n\t\tif n.MaxTimeMS > 0 && peek > n.MaxTimeMS {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !cont(peek) {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.Step()\n\t}\n}\n\n// RNG exposes the deterministic stream for fault scheduling by callers.\nfunc (n *Network) RNG() *rand.Rand { return n.rng }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":186,"oldLines":32,"newStart":186,"newLines":15,"lines":["   return s"," }"," ","-// Stats returns a snapshot of per-link counters (keys sorted for determinism).","+// Stats returns a snapshot of per-link counters."," func (n *Network) Stats() map[string]LinkStats {","   out := make(map[string]LinkStats, len(n.stats))","-  keys := make([]string, 0, len(n.stats))","   for k, s := range n.stats {","-    keys = append(keys, k)","-    st := *s","-    out[k] = st","+    out[k] = *s","   }","-  sort.Strings(keys)","-  _ = keys","   return out"," }"," ","-// schedule inserts an event.","-func (n *Network) schedule(ev Event, at int64) {","-  ev.setAt(at)","-  n.nextSeq++","-  if bp, ok := ev.(baseEventProvider); {"parentUuid":"5ab1caa4-0ddf-45d2-8966-cd6fb85e9e91","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_w4o3l55dj1ervm5uk40lirm4","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp25/b/node/node.go","content":"// Package node implements the anti-entropy engine running inside the\n// simulator: gossip partner selection, resumable sync sessions and the\n// Merkle-tree-driven difference exchange.\npackage node\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\n\t\"aesync/core\"\n\t\"aesync/proto\"\n\t\"aesync/sim\"\n)\n\n// Config is the protocol configuration shared by all nodes.\ntype Config struct {\n\t// RoundBudgetBytes bounds the bytes one session may transfer in one round\n\t// (counted on the initiator side; the responder applies the same number to\n\t// its replies).\n\tRoundBudgetBytes int64 `json:\"round_budget_bytes\"`\n\t// TickIntervalMS is the gossip cadence.\n\tTickIntervalMS int64 `json:\"tick_interval_ms\"`\n\t// TimeoutMS aborts an in-flight round when no reply arrives (lost\n\t// messages). Defaults to 5x max latency when 0.\n\tTimeoutMS int64 `json:\"timeout_ms\"`\n\t// Merkle tree shape.\n\tMerkle core.MerkleOptions `json:\"merkle\"`\n}\n\nfunc (c Config) budget() int64 {\n\tif c.RoundBudgetBytes <= 0 {\n\t\treturn 1 << 20\n\t}\n\treturn c.RoundBudgetBytes\n}\n\n// Env is the node's handle onto the simulator.\ntype Env interface {\n\tNow() int64\n\tSend(src, dst, tag string, size int64, deliver func(now int64))\n}\n\n// Counters aggregates protocol-level statistics for the run report.\ntype Counters struct {\n\tmu sync.Mutex\n\n\tRoundsStarted   int64 `json:\"rounds_started\"`\n\tRoundsResumed   int64 `json:\"rounds_resumed\"`\n\tRoundsCompleted int64 `json:\"rounds_completed\"`\n\tRoundsTimedOut  int64 `json:\"rounds_timed_out\"`\n\tSyncsCompleted  int64 `json:\"syncs_completed\"`\n\n\tNodeInfoRequests int64 `json:\"node_info_requests\"`\n\tNodeInfoReplies  int64 `json:\"node_info_replies\"`\n\tEntryRequests    int64 `json:\"entry_requests\"`\n\tEntriesBatches   int64 `json:\"entries_batches\"`\n\tEntriesSent      int64 `json:\"entries_sent\"`     // responder side\n\tEntriesApplied   int64 `json:\"entries_applied\"`  // initiator LWW accepts\n\tEntriesSkipped   int64 `json:\"entries_skipped\"`  // already current\n\tBudgetPauses     int64 `json:\"budget_pauses\"`    // rounds cut by the budget\n\tStaleMessages    int64 `json:\"stale_messages\"`   // dropped duplicates/old rounds\n\n\tBytesSent     int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesReceived int64 `json:\"bytes_received\"`\n\n\t// Efficiency metric: entries actually fetched vs. live keyspace size.\n\tLeafPrunes int64 `json:\"leaf_prunes\"`\n\tLeafDiffs  int64 `json:\"leaf_diffs\"`\n}\n\n// Node is one simulated participant.\ntype Node struct {\n\tID     string\n\tstore  *core.Store\n\tcfg    Config\n\tenv    Env\n\tnet    *sim.Network\n\tcnt    *Counters\n\n\t// sessions keyed by responder id; one active pull session per peer.\n\tsessions map[string]*session\n\n\t// gossip partner rotation\n\ttickCount int64\n\tpeers     []string // sorted\n}\n\n// New creates a node bound to a store and network.\nfunc New(id string, store *core.Store, cfg Config, net *sim.Network, cnt *Counters) *Node {\n\treturn &Node{\n\t\tID:       id,\n\t\tstore:    store,\n\t\tcfg:      cfg,\n\t\tenv:      net,\n\t\tnet:      net,\n\t\tcnt:      cnt,\n\t\tsessions: map[string]*session{},\n\t}\n}\n\n// Store exposes the node's store (for scenario setup / convergence checks).\nfunc (n *Node) Store() *core.Store { return n.store }\n\n// SetPeers fixes the gossip set.\nfunc (n *Node) SetPeers(ids []string) {\n\tps := make([]string, 0, len(ids))\n\tfor _, id := range ids {\n\t\tif id != n.ID {\n\t\t\tps = append(ps, id)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(ps)\n\tn.peers = ps\n}\n\n// Peers returns the sorted peer list.\nfunc (n *Node) Peers() []string { return n.peers }\n\n// PickPartner is the deterministic gossip choice on tick t: rotate through the\n// peer list by tick index, so every link is exercised regularly.\nfunc (n *Node) PickPartner(tick int64) string {\n\tif len(n.peers) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\treturn n.peers[int(tick)%len(n.peers)]\n}\n\n// idle reports whether the node has no in-flight round (used for convergence\n// gating and for deciding whether a tick starts a new round).\nfunc (n *Node) idleExcept(peer string) bool {\n\tfor p, s := range n.sessions {\n\t\tif p == peer {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.inFlight {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn Nodes communicate by\n// scheduling MessageEvents; user code can schedule FuncEvents (gossip ticks,\n// client writes, link partitions, link healing). Per-link behaviour —\n// latency, loss, duplication, reordering — is driven by a seeded RNG so a run\n// is fully reproducible from its JSON scenario.\npackage sim\n\nimport (\n\t\"container/heap\"\n\t\"math/rand\"\n\t\"sort\"\n)\n\n// Event is anything the clock can deliver.\ntype Event interface {\n\tAt() int64\n\tsetAt(int64)\n\tkindTag() string\n}\n\n// baseEvent carries heap bookkeeping.\ntype baseEvent struct {\n\tat int64\n\t// index lets heap.Fix/Remove work.\n\tindex int\n\t// seq ties equal timestamps apart deterministically (insertion order).\n\tseq uint64\n}\n\nfunc (e *baseEvent) At() int64      { return e.at }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) setAt(t int64)  { e.at = t }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) kindTag() string { return \"\" }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) seqVal() uint64 { return e.seq }\n\n// MessageEvent is a network message reaching dst.\ntype MessageEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tDst  string\n\tSize int64\n\t// Deliver hands the message to the destination node. It is an opaque\n\t// closure over the proto message so sim stays protocol-agnostic.\n\tDeliver func(now int64)\n\tTag     string\n}\n\nfunc (e *MessageEvent) kindTag() string { return \"msg:\" + e.Tag }\n\n// FuncEvent is a scheduled node/action callback.\ntype FuncEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tName string\n\tF    func(now int64)\n}\n\nfunc (e *FuncEvent) kindTag() string { return \"func:\" + e.Name }\n\n// eventHeap orders events by (time, insertion sequence).\ntype eventHeap []Event\n\nfunc (h eventHeap) Len() int { return len(h) }\nfunc (h eventHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {\n\ta, b := h[i].At(), h[j].At()\n\tif a != b {\n\t\treturn a < b\n\t}\n\treturn seqOf(h[i]) < seqOf(h[j])\n}\nfunc (h eventHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Push(x any)   { *h = append(*h, x.(Event)) }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Pop() any {\n\told := *h\n\tn := len(old)\n\tx := old[n-1]\n\t*h = old[:n-1]\n\treturn x\n}\n\n// seqProvider exposes the embedded baseEvent's tie-break sequence.\ntype seqProvider interface{ seqVal() uint64 }\n\nfunc seqOf(e Event) uint64 {\n\tif s, ok := e.(seqProvider); ok {\n\t\treturn s.seqVal()\n\t}\n\treturn 0\n}\n\n// LinkConfig describes one directed-ish link's fault profile. The same config\n// applies both ways (undirected edges), matching the partition model.\ntype LinkConfig struct {\n\tMinLatencyMS int64 `json:\"min_latency_ms\"`\n\tMaxLatencyMS int64 `json:\"max_latency_ms\"`\n\t// LossPct in [0,100]: probability a message copy is dropped.\n\tLossPct float64 `json:\"loss_pct\"`\n\t// DuplicatePct: probability an extra copy is scheduled.\n\tDuplicatePct float64 `json:\"duplicate_pct\"`\n\t// ReorderPct: probability a message is delayed one extra latency window,\n\t// which (combined with independent latencies) yields overtaking.\n\tReorderPct float64 `json:\"reorder_pct\"`\n}\n\n// LinkStats records traffic on one undirected link.\ntype LinkStats struct {\n\tSent      int64 `json:\"sent\"`\n\tDelivered int64 `json:\"delivered\"`\n\tLost      int64 `json:\"lost\"`\n\tDuplicated int64 `json:\"duplicated\"`\n\tBytesSent      int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesDelivered int64 `json:\"bytes_delivered\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the simulator's clock + links.\ntype Network struct {\n\trng       *rand.Rand\n\tevents    eventHeap\n\tnow       int64\n\tnextSeq   uint64\n\tlinks Nodes communicate by\n// scheduling MessageEvents; user code can schedule FuncEvents (gossip ticks,\n// client writes, link partitions, link healing). Per-link behaviour —\n// latency, loss, duplication, reordering — is driven by a seeded RNG so a run\n// is fully reproducible from its JSON scenario.\npackage sim\n\nimport (\n\t\"container/heap\"\n\t\"math/rand\"\n\t\"sort\"\n)\n\n// Event is anything the clock can deliver.\ntype Event interface {\n\tAt() int64\n\tsetAt(int64)\n\tkindTag() string\n}\n\n// baseEvent carries heap bookkeeping.\ntype baseEvent struct {\n\tat int64\n\t// index lets heap.Fix/Remove work.\n\tindex int\n\t// seq ties equal timestamps apart deterministically (insertion order).\n\tseq uint64\n}\n\nfunc (e *baseEvent) At() int64      { return e.at }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) setAt(t int64)  { e.at = t }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) kindTag() string { return \"\" }\nfunc (e *baseEvent) seqVal() uint64 { return e.seq }\n\n// MessageEvent is a network message reaching dst.\ntype MessageEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tDst  string\n\tSize int64\n\t// Deliver hands the message to the destination node. It is an opaque\n\t// closure over the proto message so sim stays protocol-agnostic.\n\tDeliver func(now int64)\n\tTag     string\n}\n\nfunc (e *MessageEvent) kindTag() string { return \"msg:\" + e.Tag }\n\n// FuncEvent is a scheduled node/action callback.\ntype FuncEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tName string\n\tF    func(now int64)\n}\n\nfunc (e *FuncEvent) kindTag() string { return \"func:\" + e.Name }\n\n// eventHeap orders events by (time, insertion sequence).\ntype eventHeap []Event\n\nfunc (h eventHeap) Len() int { return len(h) }\nfunc (h eventHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {\n\ta, b := h[i].At(), h[j].At()\n\tif a != b {\n\t\treturn a < b\n\t}\n\treturn seqOf(h[i]) < seqOf(h[j])\n}\nfunc (h eventHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Push(x any)   { *h = append(*h, x.(Event)) }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Pop() any {\n\told := *h\n\tn := len(old)\n\tx := old[n-1]\n\t*h = old[:n-1]\n\treturn x\n}\n\n// seqProvider exposes the embedded baseEvent's tie-break sequence.\ntype seqProvider interface{ seqVal() uint64 }\n\nfunc seqOf(e Event) uint64 {\n\tif s, ok := e.(seqProvider); ok {\n\t\treturn s.seqVal()\n\t}\n\treturn 0\n}\n\n// LinkConfig describes one directed-ish link's fault profile. The same config\n// applies both ways (undirected edges), matching the partition model.\ntype LinkConfig struct {\n\tMinLatencyMS int64 `json:\"min_latency_ms\"`\n\tMaxLatencyMS int64 `json:\"max_latency_ms\"`\n\t// LossPct in [0,100]: probability a message copy is dropped.\n\tLossPct float64 `json:\"loss_pct\"`\n\t// DuplicatePct: probability an extra copy is scheduled.\n\tDuplicatePct float64 `json:\"duplicate_pct\"`\n\t// ReorderPct: probability a message is delayed one extra latency window,\n\t// which (combined with independent latencies) yields overtaking.\n\tReorderPct float64 `json:\"reorder_pct\"`\n}\n\n// LinkStats records traffic on one undirected link.\ntype LinkStats struct {\n\tSent      int64 `json:\"sent\"`\n\tDelivered int64 `json:\"delivered\"`\n\tLost      int64 `json:\"lost\"`\n\tDuplicated int64 `json:\"duplicated\"`\n\tBytesSent      int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesDelivered int64 `json:\"bytes_delivered\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the simulator's clock + links.\ntype Network struct {\n\trng       *rand.Rand\n\tevents    eventHeap\n\tnow       int64\n\tnextSeq   uint64\n\tlinks     map[string]LinkConfig\n\tdownUntil map[string]int64 // undirected pair -> down until this time (-1 forever)\n\tstats     map[string]*LinkStats\n\t// pending counts messages in flight, useful for convergence gating.\n\tpending int\n\n\t// receivers maps node id to its inbound message handler.\n\treceivers map[string]func(tag string, payload []byte)\n\n\t// MaxTimeMS bounds a run defensively (0 = unlimited).\n\tMaxTimeMS int64\n}\n\n// NewNetwork creates a simulator seeded deterministically.\nfunc NewNetwork(seed int64) *Network {\n\tn := &Network{\n\t\trng:       rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed)),\n\t\tlinks:     map[string]LinkConfig{},\n\t\tdownUntil: map[string]int64{},\n\t\tstats:     map[string]*LinkStats{},\n\t}\n\tn.events = eventHeap{}\n\theap.Init(&n.events)\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// SetLink registers an undirected link between a and b.\nfunc (n *Network) SetLink(a, b string, cfg LinkConfig) {\n\tn.links[pairKey(a, b)] = cfg\n}\n\n// Partition marks the link down until at least t (t <= 0 means forever).\nfunc (n *Network) Partition(a, b string, until int64) {\n\tn.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)] = until\n}\n\n// Heal brings the link back immediately.\nfunc (n *Network) Heal(a, b string) {\n\tdelete(n.downUntil, pairKey(a, b))\n}\n\n// IsDown reports the current link state.\nfunc (n *Network) IsDown(a, b string) bool It is an opaque\n\t// closure over the proto message so sim stays protocol-agnostic.\n\tDeliver func(now int64)\n\tTag     string\n}\n\nfunc (e *MessageEvent) kindTag() string { return \"msg:\" + e.Tag }\n\n// FuncEvent is a scheduled node/action callback.\ntype FuncEvent struct {\n\tbaseEvent\n\tName string\n\tF    func(now int64)\n}\n\nfunc (e *FuncEvent) kindTag() string { return \"func:\" + e.Name }\n\n// eventHeap orders events by (time, insertion sequence).\ntype eventHeap []Event\n\nfunc (h eventHeap) Len() int { return len(h) }\nfunc (h eventHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {\n\ta, b := h[i].At(), h[j].At()\n\tif a != b {\n\t\treturn a < b\n\t}\n\treturn seqOf(h[i]) < seqOf(h[j])\n}\nfunc (h eventHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Push(x any)   { *h = append(*h, x.(Event)) }\nfunc (h *eventHeap) Pop() any {\n\told := *h\n\tn := len(old)\n\tx := old[n-1]\n\t*h = old[:n-1]\n\treturn x\n}\n\n// seqProvider exposes the embedded baseEvent's tie-break sequence.\ntype seqProvider interface{ seqVal() uint64 }\n\nfunc seqOf(e Event) uint64 {\n\tif s, ok := e.(seqProvider); ok {\n\t\treturn s.seqVal()\n\t}\n\treturn 0\n}\n\n// LinkConfig describes one directed-ish link's fault profile. The same config\n// applies both ways (undirected edges), matching the partition model.\ntype LinkConfig struct {\n\tMinLatencyMS int64 `json:\"min_latency_ms\"`\n\tMaxLatencyMS int64 `json:\"max_latency_ms\"`\n\t// LossPct in [0,100]: probability a message copy is dropped.\n\tLossPct float64 `json:\"loss_pct\"`\n\t// DuplicatePct: probability an extra copy is scheduled.\n\tDuplicatePct float64 `json:\"duplicate_pct\"`\n\t// ReorderPct: probability a message is delayed one extra latency window,\n\t// which (combined with independent latencies) yields overtaking.\n\tReorderPct float64 `json:\"reorder_pct\"`\n}\n\n// LinkStats records traffic on one undirected link.\ntype LinkStats struct {\n\tSent      int64 `json:\"sent\"`\n\tDelivered int64 `json:\"delivered\"`\n\tLost      int64 `json:\"lost\"`\n\tDuplicated int64 `json:\"duplicated\"`\n\tBytesSent      int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesDelivered int64 `json:\"bytes_delivered\"`\n}\n\n// Network is the simulator's clock + links.\ntype Network struct {\n\trng       *rand.Rand\n\tevents    eventHeap\n\tnow       int64\n\tnextSeq   uint64\n\tlinks     map[string]LinkConfig\n\tdownUntil map[string]int64 // undirected pair -> down until this time (-1 forever)\n\tstats     map[string]*LinkStats\n\t// pending counts messages in flight, useful for convergence gating.\n\tpending int\n\n\t// receivers maps node id to its inbound message handler.\n\treceivers map[string]func(tag string, payload []byte)\n\n\t// MaxTimeMS bounds a run defensively (0 = unlimited).\n\tMaxTimeMS int64\n}\n\n// NewNetwork creates a simulator seeded deterministically.\nfunc NewNetwork(seed int64) *Network {\n\tn := &Network{\n\t\trng:       rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed)),\n\t\tlinks:     map[string]LinkConfig{},\n\t\tdownUntil: map[string]int64{},\n\t\tstats:     map[string]*LinkStats{},\n\t\treceivers: map[string]func(tag string, payload []byte){},\n\t}\n\tn.events = eventHeap{}\n\theap.Init(&n.events)\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// RegisterReceiver binds a node id to its inbound handler.\nfunc (n *Network) RegisterReceiver(id string, recv func(tag string, payload []byte)) {\n\tn.receivers[id] = recv\n}\n\n// SetLink registers an undirected link between a and b.\nfunc (n *Network) SetLink(a, b string, cfg LinkConfig) {\n\tn.links[pairKey(a, b)] = cfg\n}\n\n// Partition marks the link down until at least t (t <= 0 means forever).\nfunc (n *Network) Partition(a, b string, until int64) {\n\tn.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)] = until\n}\n\n// Heal brings the link back immediately.\nfunc (n *Network) Heal(a, b string) {\n\tdelete(n.downUntil, pairKey(a, b))\n}\n\n// IsDown reports the current link state.\nfunc (n *Network) IsDown(a, b string) bool {\n\tif t, ok := n.downUntil[pairKey(a, b)]; ok {\n\t\treturn t <= 0 || n.now < t\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// Now returns the simulated time in ms.\nfunc (n *Network) Now() int64 { return n.now }\n\n// Pending reports messages currently queued for delivery.\nfunc (n *Network) Pending() int { return n.pending }\n\nfunc pairKey(a, b string) string {\n\tif a < b {\n\t\treturn a + \"\\x00\" + b\n\t}\n\treturn b + \"\\x00\" + a\n}\n\nfunc (n *Network) stat(a, b string) *LinkStats {\n\tk := pairKey(a, b)\n\ts := n.stats[k]\n\tif s == nil {\n\t\ts = &LinkStats{}\n\t\tn.stats[k] = s\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// Stats returns a snapshot of per-link counters.\nfunc (n *Network) Stats() map[string]LinkStats {\n\tout := make(map[string]LinkStats, len(n.stats))\n\tfor k, s := range n.stats {\n\t\tout[k] = *s\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// ScheduleFunc runs f at simulated time t.\nfunc (n *Network) ScheduleFunc(name string, t int64, f func(now Duplicates, loss and reordering are decided per\n// copy. On delivery the dst-registered receiver is invoked with the payload.\nfunc (n *Network) Send(src, dst, tag string, payload []byte) {\n\tsize := int64(len(payload))\n\tst := n.stat(src, dst)\n\tst.Sent++\n\tst.BytesSent += size\n\tn.pending++\n\n\tcfg := n.links[pairKey(src, dst)]\n\n\t// One \"original\" copy plus maybe a duplicate.\n\tn.scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag, payload, size, cfg, st)\n\tif cfg.DuplicatePct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.DuplicatePct {\n\t\tst.Duplicated++\n\t\tn.scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag, payload, size, cfg, st)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *Network) scheduleCopy(src, dst, tag string, payload []byte, size int64,\n\tcfg LinkConfig, st *LinkStats) {\n\n\tif n.IsDown(src, dst) {\n\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif cfg.LossPct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.LossPct {\n\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tlat := cfg.MinLatencyMS\n\tif cfg.MaxLatencyMS > lat {\n\t\tlat += n.rng.Int63n(cfg.MaxLatencyMS - lat + 1)\n\t}\n\tif lat < 0 {\n\t\tlat = 0\n\t}\n\tif cfg.ReorderPct > 0 && n.rng.Float64()*100 < cfg.ReorderPct {\n\t\t// Push this copy late enough that later-sent messages overtake it.\n\t\tlat += cfg.MaxLatencyMS + 1\n\t}\n\tat := n.now + lat\n\tev := &MessageEvent{Dst: dst, Size: size, Tag: tag}\n\tn.nextSeq++\n\tev.baseEvent.seq = n.nextSeq\n\tbody := append([]byte(nil), payload...)\n\tev.Deliver = func(now int64) {\n\t\t// A link may fail while the message is in flight: re-check on delivery.\n\t\tif n.IsDown(src, dst) {\n\t\t\tst.Lost++\n\t\t\tn.pending--\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tst.Delivered++\n\t\tst.BytesDelivered += size\n\t\tn.pending--\n\t\tif recv := n.receivers[dst]; recv != nil {\n\t\t\trecv(tag, body)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tev.setAt(at)\n\theap.Push(&n.events, ev)\n}\n\n// Step advances one event. It returns false when no events remain (or the\n// defensive time bound is hit).\nfunc (n *Network) Step() bool {\n\tif n.events.Len() == 0 {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tev := heap.Pop(&n.events).(Event)\n\tif n.MaxTimeMS > 0 && ev.At() > n.MaxTimeMS {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tn.now = ev.At()\n\tswitch e := ev.(type) {\n\tcase *MessageEvent:\n\t\te.Deliver(n.now)\n\tcase *FuncEvent:\n\t\te.F(n.now)\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// RunUntilIdle processes all events.\nfunc (n *Network) RunUntilIdle() {\n\tfor n.Step() {\n\t}\n}\n\n// Run processes events while cont() returns true (or until idle).\nfunc (n *Network) Run(cont func(now int64) bool) {\n\tfor n.events.Len() > 0 {\n\t\tpeek := n.events[0].At()\n\t\tif n.MaxTimeMS > 0 && peek > n.MaxTimeMS {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !cont(peek) {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.Step()\n\t}\n}\n\n// RNG exposes the deterministic stream for fault scheduling by callers.\nfunc (n *Network) RNG() *rand.Rand { return n.rng }\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":10,"oldLines":7,"newStart":10,"newLines":6,"lines":[" import (","   \"container/heap\"","   \"math/rand\"","-  \"sort\""," )"," "," // Event is anything the clock can deliver."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a7e5e148-8ced-4908-a242-ba21ed8eebea","session_id":"6ceb46e9-51b0-4732-85e2-22ec4d062a75","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp25/b","sessionId":"6ceb46e9-51b0-4732-85e2-22ec4d062a75","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp25-b","slug":"happy-sleeping-aurora"}

net,\n\t\tnet:      net,\n\t\tcnt:      cnt,\n\t\tsessions: map[string]*session{},\n\t}\n}\n\n// Store exposes the node's store (for scenario setup / convergence checks).\nfunc (n *Node) Store() *core.Store { return n.store }\n\n// SetPeers fixes the gossip set.\nfunc (n *Node) SetPeers(ids []string) {\n\tps := make([]string, 0, len(ids))\n\tfor _, id := range ids {\n\t\tif id != n.ID {\n\t\t\tps = append(ps, id)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(ps)\n\tn.peers = ps\n}\n\n// Peers returns the sorted peer list.\nfunc (n *Node) Peers() []string { return n.peers }\n\n// PickPartner is the the responder applies the same number to\n\t// its replies).\n\tRoundBudgetBytes int64 `json:\"round_budget_bytes\"`\n\t// TickIntervalMS is the gossip cadence.\n\tTickIntervalMS int64 `json:\"tick_interval_ms\"`\n\t// TimeoutMS aborts an in-flight round when no reply arrives (lost\n\t// messages). Defaults to 5x max latency when 0.\n\tTimeoutMS int64 `json:\"timeout_ms\"`\n\t// Merkle tree shape.\n\tMerkle core.MerkleOptions `json:\"merkle\"`\n}\n\nfunc (c Config) budget() int64 {\n\tif c.RoundBudgetBytes <= 0 {\n\t\treturn 1 << 20\n\t}\n\treturn c.RoundBudgetBytes\n}\n\n// Node is one simulated participant.\ntype Node struct {\n\tID     string\n\tstore  *core.Store\n\tcfg    Config\n\tnet    *sim.Network\n\tcnt    *Counters\n\n\t// sessions keyed by responder id; one active pull session per peer.\n\tsessions map[string]*session\n\n\t// gossip partner rotation\n\ttickCount int64\n\tpeers     []string // sorted\n}\n\n// New creates a node bound to a store and network.\nfunc New(id string, store *core.Store, cfg Config, net *sim.Network, cnt *Counters) *Node {\n\tn := payload []byte) {\n\t\tm, err := proto.Decode(payload)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.deliver(m)\n\t})\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// Store exposes the node's store (for scenario setup / convergence checks).\nfunc (n *Node) Store() *core.Store { return n.store }\n\n// SetPeers fixes the gossip set.\nfunc (n *Node) SetPeers(ids []string) {\n\tps := make([]string, 0, len(ids))\n\tfor _, id := range ids {\n\t\tif id != n.ID {\n\t\t\tps = append(ps, id)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(ps)\n\tn.peers = ps\n}\n\n// Peers returns the sorted peer list.\nfunc (n *Node) Peers() []string { return n.peers }\n\n// PickPartner is the deterministic gossip choice on tick t: rotate through the\n// peer list by tick index, so every link is exercised regularly.\nfunc (n *Node) PickPartner(tick int64) string {\n\tif len(n.peers) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\treturn n.peers[int(tick)%len(n.peers)]\n}\n\n// idle reports whether the node has no in-flight round (used for convergence\n// gating and for deciding whether a tick starts a new round).\nfunc (n *Node) idleExcept(peer string) bool {\n\tfor p, s := range n.sessions {\n\t\tif p == peer {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.inFlight {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// allIdle reports no in-flight rounds to any peer.\nfunc (n *Node) allIdle() bool {\n\tfor _, s := range n.sessions {\n\t\tif s.inFlight {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) send(to string, env *proto.Envelope) {\n\tsize := env.EncodeSize()\n\tn.cnt.addBytesSent(size)\n\tpayload, _ := json.Marshal(env)\n\tn.net.Send(n.ID, to, env.Type, size, func(_ int64) {\n\t\tvar got proto.Envelope\n\t\tif err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &got); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.deliver(&got)\n\t})\n}\n\n// deliver routes an inbound envelope either to the responder logic (begin) or\n// to the owning session.\nfunc (n *Node) deliver(m *proto.Envelope) {\n\tn.cnt.addBytesReceived(m.EncodeSize())\n\n\t// Replies arriving at the initiator.\n\tif m.Initiator == n.ID {\n\t\ts := n.sessions[m.Peer]\n\t\tif s == nil {\n\t\t\tn.cnt.addStale()\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif m.Round != s.round {\n\t\t\tn.cnt.addStale()\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\ts.handleReply(m)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// Requests arriving at the responder.\n\tif m.Type == proto.TypeSyncBegin {\n\t\tn.handleBegin(m)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\t// Other request types without a begin are unexpected.\n\tn.cnt.addStale()\n}\n\n// logf is a tiny debug hook disabled by default.\nfunc (n *Node) logf(format string, args ...any) {\n\tif debugEnabled {\n\t\tfmt.Printf(\"[t=%d %s] \", n.env.Now(), n.ID)\n\t\tfmt.Printf(format+\"\\n\", args...)\n\t}\n}\n\nvar debugEnabled = false\n\n// SetDebug toggles verbose protocol logging.\nfunc SetDebug(on bool) { debugEnabled = on  int64 `json:\"syncs_completed\"`\n\n\tNodeInfoRequests int64 `json:\"node_info_requests\"`\n\tNodeInfoReplies  int64 `json:\"node_info_replies\"`\n\tEntryRequests    int64 `json:\"entry_requests\"`\n\tEntriesBatches   int64 `json:\"entries_batches\"`\n\tEntriesSent      int64 `json:\"entries_sent\"`    // responder side\n\tEntriesApplied   int64 `json:\"entries_applied\"` // initiator LWW accepts\n\tEntriesSkipped   int64 `json:\"entries_skipped\"` // already current\n\tBudgetPauses     int64 `json:\"budget_pauses\"`   // rounds cut by the budget\n\tStaleMessages    int64 `json:\"stale_messages\"`  // dropped duplicates/old rounds\n\n\tBytesSent     int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesReceived int64 `json:\"bytes_received\"`\n\n\t// sessions keyed by responder id; one active pull session per peer.\n\tsessions map[string]*session\n\n\t// gossip partner rotation\n\ttickCount int64\n\tpeers     []string // sorted\n}\n\n// New creates a node bound to a store and network.\nfunc New(id string, store *core.Store, cfg Config, net *sim.Network, cnt *Counters) *Node {\n\tn := &Node{\n\t\tID:       id,\n\t\tstore:    store,\n\t\tcfg:      cfg,\n\t\tnet:      net,\n\t\tcnt:      cnt,\n\t\tsessions: map[string]*session{},\n\t}\n\tnet.RegisterReceiver(id, func(tag string, payload []byte) {\n\t\tm, err := proto.Decode(payload)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.deliver(m)\n\t})\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// Store exposes the node's store (for scenario setup / convergence checks).\nfunc (n *Node) Store() *core.Store { return n.store }\n\n// SetPeers fixes the gossip set.\nfunc (n *Node) SetPeers(ids []string) {\n\tps := make([]string, 0, len(ids))\n\tfor _, id := range ids {\n\t\tif id != n.ID {\n\t\t\tps = append(ps, id)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(ps)\n\tn.peers = ps\n}\n\n// Peers returns the sorted peer list.\nfunc (n *Node) Peers() []string { return n.peers }\n\n// PickPartner is the deterministic gossip choice on tick t: rotate through the\n// peer list by tick index, so every link is exercised regularly.\nfunc (n *Node) PickPartner(tick int64) string {\n\tif len(n.peers) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\treturn n.peers[int(tick)%len(n.peers)]\n}\n\n// idle reports whether the node has no in-flight round (used for convergence\n// gating and for deciding whether a tick starts When Keys\n// is empty the responder sends the whole segment (used for a leaf-vs-leaf\n// comparison after summaries already established the differing key set; the\n// initiator always lists the exact keys it wants, so segment-pull still only\n// moves differing records).\ntype EntriesReq struct {\n\tPrefix string   `json:\"prefix\"`\n\tKeys   []string `json:\"keys\"`\n}\n\n// Entries is one batch of full entries (tombstones included). Final marks the\n// last batch of one EntriesReq response; Done marks the whole walk complete\n// (informational; SyncEnd is the authoritative close).\ntype Entries struct {\n\tPrefix string       `json:\"prefix\"`\n\tItems  []core.Entry `json:\"items\"`\n\tFinal  bool         `json:\"final\"`\n}\n\n// EncodeSize is the exact on-wire JSON size of an envelope.\nfunc (m *Envelope) EncodeSize() int64 {\n\tb, err := json.Marshal(m)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\treturn int64(len(b))\n}\n\n// Decode parses an envelope from JSON.\nfunc Decode(data []byte) (*Envelope, error) {\n\tvar m Envelope\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(data, &m); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn &m, nil\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_9e417eaac012a31ecb1d769a","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":2905,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":61240,"output_tokens":1115,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_8z438qjcdgv7e15at6wuloyo":{"content":"// Package proto defines the messages exchanged by anti-entropy peers and the\n// accounting rules for the per-round communication budget.\n//\n// Protocol (one pull round, initiator A pulls from responder B):\n//\n//\tA -> B : SyncBegin {round, budget}\n//\tB      : builds a fresh Merkle tree of its log\n//\tA <-> B: request/response walk of the tree.\n//\t         A asks for NodeInfo(prefix) or Entries(prefix); The receiver\n// drops messages whose round differs from the one it knows about, which makes\n// duplicates and late messages from a dead round harmless.\npackage proto\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\n\t\"aesync/core\"\n)\n\n// Message types.\nconst (\n\tTypeSyncBegin    = \"sync_begin\"    // initiator -> responder\n\tTypeSyncEnd      = \"sync_end\"      // initiator -> responder, round done\n\tTypeNodeInfoReq  = \"node_info_req\" // initiator -> responder\n\tTypeNodeInfoResp = \"node_info_resp\"\n\tTypeEntriesReq   = \"entries_req\"\n\tTypeEntriesResp  = \"entries_resp\"\n)\n\n// Envelope wraps one message with the routing/identity fields.\ntype Envelope struct {\n\tType      string `json:\"type\"`\n\tSession   string `json:\"session\"`\n\tInitiator string `json:\"initiator\"`\n\tPeer      string `json:\"peer\"`\n\tRound     int64  `json:\"round\"`\n\n\tBegin *SyncBegin `json:\"begin,omitempty\"`\n\tEnd   *SyncEnd   `json:\"end,omitempty\"`\n\tNReq  *NodeReq   `json:\"nreq,omitempty\"`\n\tNResp *NodeResp  `json:\"nresp,omitempty\"`\n\tEReq  *EntriesReq `json:\"ereq,omitempty\"`\n\tEResp *Entries   `json:\"eresp,omitempty\"`\n}\n\n// SyncBegin opens (or resumes after a network gap) a round.\ntype SyncBegin struct {\n\tBudgetBytes int64 `json:\"budget_bytes\"`\n}\n\n// SyncEnd tells the responder its ephemeral tree can be dropped.\ntype SyncEnd struct{}\n\n// NodeReq asks for the responder's node description at Prefix.\ntype NodeReq struct {\n\tPrefix string `json:\"prefix\"`\n}\n\n// NodeResp is the responder's node description.\ntype NodeResp struct {\n\tPrefix string        `json:\"prefix\"`\n\tNode   core.NodeInfo `json:\"node\"`\n}\n\n// EntriesReq asks for full entries under Prefix restricted to Keys. When Keys\n// is empty the responder sends the whole segment (used for a leaf-vs-leaf\n// comparison after summaries already established the differing key set; the\n// initiator always lists the exact keys it wants, so segment-pull still only\n// moves differing records).\ntype EntriesReq struct {\n\tPrefix string   `json:\"prefix\"`\n\tKeys   []string `json:\"keys\"`\n}\n\n// Entries is one batch of full entries (tombstones included). Final marks the\n// last batch of one EntriesReq response; Done marks the whole walk complete\n// (informational; SyncEnd is the authoritative close).\ntype Entries struct {\n\tPrefix string       `json:\"prefix\"`\n\tItems  []core.Entry `json:\"items\"`\n\tFinal  bool         `json:\"final\"`\n}\n\n// EncodeSize is the exact on-wire JSON size of an envelope.\nfunc (m *Envelope) EncodeSize() int64 {\n\tb, err := json.Marshal(m)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\treturn int64(len(b))\n}\n\n// Decode parses an envelope from JSON.\nfunc Decode(data []byte) (*Envelope, error) {\n\tvar m Envelope\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(data, &m); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn &m, nil\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":5,"newStart":1,"newLines":19,"lines":[" // Package proto defines the messages exchanged by anti-entropy peers and the"," // accounting rules for the per-round communication budget.","+//","+// Protocol (one pull round, initiator A pulls from responder B):","+//","+//\tA -> B : SyncBegin {round, budget}","+//\tB      : builds a fresh Merkle tree of its log","+//\tA <-> B: request/response walk of the tree.","+//\t         A asks for NodeInfo(prefix) or Entries(prefix); B answers.","+//\t         The walk state (stack of prefixes, leaf cursors, wanted keys)","+//\t         lives on A and survives between rounds, so a round cut off by the","+//\t         byte budget or a partition resumes where it stopped.","+//","+// Every envelope carries session id, initiator, peer and round. Used for both the","-// communication budget and traffic statistics.","+// EncodeSize is the exact on-wire JSON size of an envelope."," func (m *Envelope) EncodeSize() int64 {","   b, err := json.Marshal(m)","   if err != nil {","-    // Messages only contain JSON-safe types; treat as 0 if it ever fails.","     return 0","   }","   return int64(len(b))"]}],"originalFile":"// Package proto defines the messages exchanged by anti-entropy peers and the\n// accounting rules for the per-round communication budget.\npackage proto\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\n\t\"aesync/core\"\n)\n\n// Message types.\nconst (\n\tTypeSyncBegin = \"sync_begin\" // initiator -> responder, starts/resumes a round\n\tTypeNodeInfo  = \"node_info\"  // responder -> initiator, Merkle node description\n\tTypeEntries   = \"entries\"    // responder -> initiator, full entries for wanted keys\n)\n\n// Envelope wraps one message with the session identity both sides need to\n// route it. Round is the initiator's current round number; stale messages\n// (from an aborted round / duplicate) are dropped by the receiver.\ntype Envelope struct {\n\tType      string `json:\"type\"`\n\tSession   string `json:\"session\"`\n\tInitiator string `json:\"initiator\"`\n\tPeer      string `json:\"peer\"`\n\tRound     int64  `json:\"round\"`\n\n\tBegin *SyncBegin `json:\"begin,omitempty\"`\n\tInfo  *NodeInfo  `json:\"info,omitempty\"`\n\tData  *Entries   `json:\"data,omitempty\"`\n}\n\n// SyncBegin opens a round. The responder replies from its current tree.\ntype SyncBegin struct {\n\tBudgetBytes int64 `json:\"budget_bytes\"`\n}\n\n// NodeInfo carries one Merkle node plus the prefix it answers.\ntype NodeInfo struct {\n\tPrefix string         `json:\"prefix\"`\n\tNode   core.NodeInfo  `json:\"node\"`\n}\n\n// Entries is a batch of full key entries (tombstones included). Final marks\n// the last batch of the response stream for one request phase.\ntype Entries struct {\n\tItems []core.Entry `json:\"items\"`\n\tFinal bool         `json:\"final\"`\n}\n\n// EncodeSize is the exact on-wire JSON size of an envelope. Used for both the\n// communication budget and traffic statistics.\nfunc (m *Envelope) EncodeSize() int64 {\n\tb, err := json.Marshal(m)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\t// Messages only contain JSON-safe types; treat as 0 if it ever fails.\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\treturn int64(len(b))\n}\n\n// Decode parses an envelope from JSON.\nfunc Decode(data []byte) (*Envelope, error) {\n\tvar m Envelope\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(data, &m); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn &m, nil\n}\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d3308a4f-48ab-43b8-9b00-49e01c3aa620","session_id":"6ceb46e9-51b0-4732-85e2-22ec4d062a75","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp25/b","sessionId":"6ceb46e9-51b0-4732-85e2-22ec4d062a75","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp25-b","slug":"happy-sleeping-aurora"}

{"parentUuid":"972b5325-d3e6-430d-9954-3e0c56468252","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_506h0ki8bvh9m6r8titsoglp","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp25/b/node/node.go","content":"// Package node implements the anti-entropy engine running inside the\n// simulator: gossip partner selection, resumable pull sessions and the\n// Merkle-tree-driven difference exchange.\n//\n// Walk model\n//\n// The initiator owns a work stack of Merkle prefixes. On each reply it\n// compares its node at a prefix with the responder's, pushes children whose\n// digests differ, and at leaves performs an ordered merge of item summaries to\n// enumerate exactly the keys whose full records (value or tombstone) must be\n// pulled. Equal leaves are pruned without any record transfer.\n//\n// Resumability\n//\n// All walk state (stack, pending requests, per-round byte usage) lives on the\n// initiator's session object. A round cut off by the per-round budget, by a\n// partition or by message loss simply pauses; the next gossip tick starts a\n// new round against the same session and the walk continues from its stack.\npackage node\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\n\t\"aesync/core\"\n\t\"aesync/proto\"\n\t\"aesync/sim\"\n)\n\n// Config is the protocol configuration shared by all nodes.\ntype Config struct {\n\t// RoundBudgetBytes bounds the bytes one round may transfer. Both request\n\t// and response bytes count against it (counted on the initiator side; the\n\t// responder independently caps its reply batches to the same budget).\n\tRoundBudgetBytes int64 `json:\"round_budget_bytes\"`\n\t// TickIntervalMS is the gossip cadence.\n\tTickIntervalMS int64 `json:\"tick_interval_ms\"`\n\t// TimeoutMS aborts an in-flight round when no reply arrives (lost\n\t// messages). 0 disables timeouts (relying on ticks alone).\n\tTimeoutMS int64 `json:\"timeout_ms\"`\n\t// BatchOverheadBytes reserves envelope/JSON overhead in batch budgeting.\n\tBatchOverheadBytes int64 `json:\"batch_overhead_bytes\"`\n\t// Merkle tree shape.\n\tMerkle core.MerkleOptions `json:\"merkle\"`\n}\n\nfunc (c Config) budget() int64 {\n\tif c.RoundBudgetBytes <= 0 {\n\t\treturn 1 << 20\n\t}\n\treturn c.RoundBudgetBytes\n}\n\nfunc (c Config) overhead() int64 {\n\tif c.BatchOverheadBytes <= 0 {\n\t\treturn 128\n\t}\n\treturn c.BatchOverheadBytes\n}\n\n// Counters aggregates protocol-level statistics for the run report. Updates\n// happen from the single simulator goroutine; the mutex guards external reads.\ntype Counters struct {\n\tmu sync.Mutex\n\n\tRoundsStarted   int64 `json:\"rounds_started\"`\n\tRoundsResumed   int64 `json:\"rounds_resumed\"`\n\tRoundsCompleted int64 `json:\"rounds_completed\"`\n\tRoundsTimedOut  int64 `json:\"rounds_timed_out\"`\n\tSyncsCompleted  int64 `json:\"syncs_completed\"`\n\n\tNodeInfoRequests int64 `json:\"node_info_requests\"`\n\tNodeInfoReplies  int64 `json:\"node_info_replies\"`\n\tEntryRequests    int64 `json:\"entry_requests\"`\n\tEntriesBatches   int64 `json:\"entries_batches\"`\n\tEntriesSent      int64 `json:\"entries_sent\"`\n\tEntriesApplied   int64 `json:\"entries_applied\"`\n\tEntriesSkipped   int64 `json:\"entries_skipped\"`\n\tBudgetPauses     int64 `json:\"budget_pauses\"`\n\tStaleMessages    int64 `json:\"stale_messages\"`\n\n\tBytesSent     int64 `json:\"bytes_sent\"`\n\tBytesReceived int64 `json:\"bytes_received\"`\n\n\tLeafPrunes int64 `json:\"leaf_prunes\"`\n\tLeafDiffs  int64 `json:\"leaf_diffs\"`\n}\n\n// Snapshot returns a copy of the counters.\nfunc (c *Counters) Snapshot() Counters {\n\tc.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer c.mu.Unlock()\n\treturn *c\n}\n\nfunc (c *Counters) inc(f func(*Counters)) { f(c) }\n\n// Node is one simulated participant.\ntype Node struct {\n\tID    string\n\tstore *core.Store\n\tcfg   Config\n\tnet   *sim.Network\n\tcnt   *Counters\n\n\t// initiator-side pull sessions, keyed by responder id.\n\tsessions map[string]*session\n\t// responder-side ephemeral state keyed by session id.\n\trespState map[string]*responderState\n\n\tpeers []string // sorted\n}\n\n// responderState is what the responder remembers for one open round.\ntype responderState struct {\n\tinitiator string\n\tround     int64\n\tbudget    int64\n\ttree      *core.Tree\n}\n\n// New creates a node bound to a store and network and registers its receiver.\nfunc New(id string, store *core.Store, cfg Config, net *sim.Network, cnt *Counters) *Node {\n\tn := &Node{\n\t\tID:        id,\n\t\tstore:     store,\n\t\tcfg:       cfg,\n\t\tnet:       net,\n\t\tcnt:       cnt,\n\t\tsessions:  map[string]*session{},\n\t\trespState: map[string]*responderState{},\n\t}\n\tnet.RegisterReceiver(id, func(_ string, payload []byte) {\n\t\tm, err := proto.Decode(payload)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.deliver(m)\n\t})\n\treturn n\n}\n\n// Store exposes the node's store.\nfunc (n *Node) Store() *core.Store { return n.store }\n\n// SetPeers fixes the gossip set.\nfunc (n *Node) SetPeers(ids []string) {\n\tps := make([]string, 0, len(ids))\n\tfor _, id := range ids {\n\t\tif id != n.ID {\n\t\t\tps = append(ps, id)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(ps)\n\tn.peers = ps\n}\n\n// Peers returns the sorted peer list.\nfunc (n *Node) Peers() []string { return n.peers }\n\n// PickPartner is the deterministic gossip choice on tick t: round-robin over\n// the peer list so every link is exercised regularly.\nfunc (n *Node) PickPartner(tick int64) string {\n\tif len(n.peers) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\treturn n.peers[int(tick)%len(n.peers)]\n}\n\n// AllIdle reports no in-flight initiator rounds.\nfunc (n *Node) AllIdle() bool {\n\tfor _, s := range n.sessions {\n\t\tif s.inFlight {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) send(to string, env *proto.Envelope) {\n\tpayload, err := json.Marshal(env)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tn.cnt.mu.Lock()\n\tn.cnt.BytesSent += int64(len(payload))\n\tn.cnt.mu.Unlock()\n\tn.net.Send(n.ID, to, env.Type, payload)\n}\n\n// deliver routes inbound envelopes to initiator sessions or responder logic.\nfunc (n *Node) deliver(m *proto.Envelope) {\n\tn.cnt.mu.Lock()\n\tn.cnt.BytesReceived += m.EncodeSize()\n\tn.cnt.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tif m.Initiator == n.ID {\n\t\t// Reply to one of our pull sessions.\n\t\ts := n.sessions[m.Peer]\n\t\tif s == nil || m.Round != s.round {\n\t\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.StaleMessages++ })\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\ts.onReply(n, m)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// Requests we must answer as responder.\n\tswitch m.Type {\n\tcase proto.TypeSyncBegin:\n\t\tn.handleBegin(m)\n\tcase proto.TypeNodeInfoReq:\n\t\tn.handleNodeInfoReq(m)\n\tcase proto.TypeEntriesReq:\n\t\tn.handleEntriesReq(m)\n\tcase proto.TypeSyncEnd:\n\t\tdelete(n.respState, m.Session)\n\tdefault:\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.StaleMessages++ })\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) count(f func(c *Counters)) {\n\tn.cnt.mu.Lock()\n\tf(n.cnt)\n\tn.cnt.mu.Unlock()\n}\n\n// ---------- responder side ----------\n\nfunc (n *Node) handleBegin(m *proto.Envelope) {\n\tbudget := n.cfg.budget()\n\tif m.Begin != nil && m.Begin.BudgetBytes > 0 {\n\t\tbudget = m.Begin.BudgetBytes\n\t}\n\t// A fresh tree every round: cheap, and immune to stale responder state.\n\tn.respState[m.Session] = &responderState{\n\t\tinitiator: m.Initiator,\n\t\tround:     m.Round,\n\t\tbudget:    budget,\n\t\ttree:      core.BuildTree(n.store.AllEntries(), n.cfg.Merkle),\n\t}\n\tinfo := n.respState[m.Session].tree.Info(\"\")\n\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.NodeInfoReplies++ })\n\tn.send(m.Initiator, &proto.Envelope{\n\t\tType: proto.TypeNodeInfoResp, Session: m.Session,\n\t\tInitiator: m.Initiator, Peer: n.ID, Round: m.Round,\n\t\tNResp: &proto.NodeResp{Prefix: \"\", Node: info},\n\t})\n}\n\n// currentRound validates that an inbound request belongs to a live round.\nfunc (n *Node) currentRound(m *proto.Envelope) (*responderState, bool) {\n\tst, ok := n.respState[m.Session]\n\tif !ok || st.round != m.Round || st.initiator != m.Initiator {\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.StaleMessages++ })\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\treturn st, true\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) handleNodeInfoReq(m *proto.Envelope) {\n\tst, ok := currentRound(n, m)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tprefix := \"\"\n\tif m.NReq != nil {\n\t\tprefix = m.NReq.Prefix\n\t}\n\tinfo := st.tree.Info(prefix)\n\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.NodeInfoReplies++ })\n\tn.send(m.Initiator, &proto.Envelope{\n\t\tType: proto.TypeNodeInfoResp, Session: m.Session,\n\t\tInitiator: m.Initiator, Peer: n.ID, Round: m.Round,\n\t\tNResp: &proto.NodeResp{Prefix: prefix, Node: info},\n\t})\n}\n\nfunc (n *Node) handleEntriesReq(m *proto.Envelope) {\n\tst, ok := currentRound(n, m)\n\tif !ok || m.EReq == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.EntriesBatches++ })\n\n\t// Gather requested records. A session that never completed\n// continues; a completed one starts a fresh verification walk.\nfunc (n *Node) Tick(now int64) {\n\tn.tickCount++\n\tpeer := n.PickPartner(n.tickCount - 1)\n\tif peer == \"\" {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\ts := n.sessions[peer]\n\tif s == nil {\n\t\ts = newSession(n.ID, peer)\n\t\tn.sessions[peer] = s\n\t}\n\tif s.inFlight {\n\t\t// Previous round still running; let the timeout decide its fate.\n\t\tif n.cfg.TimeoutMS > 0 && now > s.deadline {\n\t\t\ts.abortRound(n, now, true)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\ts.startRound(n, now)\n}\n\n// tickCount accessor for tests.\nfunc (n *Node) tickIndex() int64 { return n.tickCount }\n\nfunc (s *session) startRound(n *Node, now int64) {\n\ts.round++\n\ts.phase = phaseAwaitRoot\n\ts.inFlight = true\n\ts.bytesUsed = 0\n\ts.budget = n.cfg.budget()\n\ts.pending = nil\n\t// A resumed walk keeps its stack; only a completed sync restarts from \"\".\n\tif len(s.stack) == 0 && s.phase != phaseAwaitRoot {\n\t\ts.stack = []frame{{prefix: \"\"}}\n\t}\n\tif s.round == 1 {\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.RoundsStarted++ })\n\t} else {\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) {\n\t\t\tc.RoundsStarted++\n\t\t\tif len(s.stack) > 0 {\n\t\t\t\tc.RoundsResumed++\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tenv := &proto.Envelope{\n\t\tType: proto.TypeSyncBegin, Session: s.sessionID,\n\t\tInitiator: n.ID, Peer: s.peer, Round: s.round,\n\t\tBegin: &proto.SyncBegin{BudgetBytes: s.budget},\n\t}\n\ts.charge(n, env)\n\tn.send(s.peer, env)\n\ts.armTimeout(n, now)\n}\n\nfunc (s *session) armTimeout(n *Node, now int64) {\n\tif n.cfg.TimeoutMS <= 0 {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\ts.deadline = now + n.cfg.TimeoutMS\n}\n\n// abortRound drops the in-flight round, returning any pending request to the\n// work stack so the next round resumes. timedOut distinguishes loss from a\n// budget cut (budget pauses schedule no immediate retry; the next tick does).\nfunc (s *session) abortRound(n *Node, now int64, timedOut bool) {\n\tif s.pending != nil {\n\t\t// Re-queue the unfinished prefix at the top of the stack.\n\t\ts.stack = append(s.stack, frame{prefix: s.pending.prefix})\n\t\ts.pending = nil\n\t}\n\ts.inFlight = false\n\ts.phase = phaseIdle\n\tif timedOut {\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.RoundsTimedOut++ })\n\t}\n}\n\n// pauseByBudget ends the round because the byte budget was reached. Walk state\n// is preserved verbatim; the next tick resumes.\nfunc (s *session) pauseByBudget(n *Node) {\n\tif s.pending != nil {\n\t\ts.stack = append(s.stack, frame{prefix: s.pending.prefix})\n\t\ts.pending = nil\n\t}\n\ts.inFlight = false\n\ts.phase = phaseIdle\n\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.BudgetPauses++ })\n}\n\n// onReply dispatches a reply matching the current round.\nfunc (s *session) onReply(n *Node, m *proto.Envelope) {\n\tswitch m.Type {\n\tcase proto.TypeNodeInfoResp:\n\t\ts.handleNodeInfo(n, m)\n\tcase proto.TypeEntriesResp:\n\t\ts.handleEntries(n, m)\n\tdefault:\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.StaleMessages++ })\n\t}\n}\n\n// localTree builds the initiator's current tree for comparison.\nfunc (n *Node) localTree() *core.Tree {\n\treturn core.BuildTree(n.store.AllEntries(), n.cfg.Merkle)\n}\n\nfunc (s *session) charge(n *Node, env *proto.Envelope) {\n\ts.bytesUsed += env.EncodeSize()\n}\n\nfunc (s *session) budgetExhausted() bool {\n\treturn s.bytesUsed >= s.budget\n}\n\n// ---------- walk ----------\n\n// continueWalk drives the request/response loop while budget allows. It runs\n// synchronously after each reply because the simulator is single-threaded;\n// when a request must be sent and a reply awaited, it stops.\nfunc (s *session) continueWalk(n *Node) {\n\ttree := n.localTree()\n\tfor {\n\t\tif s.pending != nil {\n\t\t\t// Waiting for a reply; nothing more to do this round.\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif len(s.stack) == 0 {\n\t\t\ts.complete(n)\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif s.budgetExhausted() {\n\t\t\ts.pauseByBudget(n)\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttop := s.stack[len(s.stack)-1]\n\t\ts.stack = s.stack[:len(s.stack)-1]\n\n\t\tlocal := tree.Info(top.prefix)\n\t\t// We need the responder's view of this prefix before deciding.\n\t\treq := &proto.Envelope{\n\t\t\tType: proto.TypeNodeInfoReq, Session: s.sessionID,\n\t\t\tInitiator: n.ID, Peer: s.peer, Round: s.round,\n\t\t\tNReq: &proto.NodeReq{Prefix: top.prefix},\n\t\t}\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.NodeInfoRequests++ })\n\t\ts.charge(n, req)\n\t\ts.pending = &pendingReq{kind: proto.TypeNodeInfoReq, prefix: top.prefix}\n\t\tn.send(s.peer, req)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n}\n\n// handleNodeInfo processes the responder's description of the pending prefix.\nfunc (s *session) handleNodeInfo(n *Node, m *proto.Envelope) {\n\ts.charge(n, m)\n\tif s.pending == nil || s.pending.kind != proto.TypeNodeInfoReq {\n\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.StaleMessages++ })\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tprefix := s.pending.prefix\n\ts.pending = nil\n\n\ttree := n.localTree()\n\tlocal := tree.Info(prefix)\n\tremote := m.NResp.Node\n\n\t// Normalize structural divergence: when one side is internal and the\n\t// other's node is a leaf (or empty), both views are flattened to leaf\n\t// summaries at the common prefix and compared directly.\n\tif local.Kind == remote.Kind {\n\t\tif local.Kind == core.KindEmpty {\n\t\t\ts.afterEqualPrefix(n)\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tif local.Kind == core.KindLeaf {\n\t\t\ts.compareLeaves(n, prefix, local.Items, remote.Items)\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\ts.compareInternal(n, prefix, local.Children, remote.Children)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// Mixed kinds: flatten both sides over the prefix.\n\tvar localItems, remoteItems []core.ItemSummary\n\tif local.Kind == core.KindLeaf {\n\t\tlocalItems = local.Items\n\t} else {\n\t\tlocalItems = flattenSummaries(tree.EntriesUnder(prefix))\n\t}\n\tif remote.Kind == core.KindLeaf {\n\t\tremoteItems = remote.Items\n\t} else {\n\t\tremoteItems = flattenSummaries(n.entriesOfRemote(prefix, remote))\n\t}\n\ts.compareLeaves(n, prefix, localItems, remoteItems)\n}\n\nfunc flattenSummaries(entries []core.Entry) []core.ItemSummary {\n\tout := make([]core.ItemSummary, len(entries))\n\tfor i, e := range entries {\n\t\tout[i] = core.ItemSummary{Key: e.Key, Version: e.Version, Deleted: e.Deleted}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// entriesOfRemote reconstructs entries from the remote node's leaf items; for\n// flattening we only need summaries, and the remote NodeInfo in the mixed case\n// carries an internal node — but the responder flattened to a leaf whenever\n// the initiator asked a prefix it didn't have as a boundary. In the reverse\n// divergence (responder internal, local leaf) we must walk the remote\n// subtree; that is handled by compareInternal's flattening branch requesting\n// the segment directly, so this helper only deals with leaf/empty remote.\nfunc (n *Node) entriesOfRemote(prefix string, node core.NodeInfo) []core.Entry {\n\t// node is internal here in theory; return nothing and rely on caller path\n\t// (compareInternal) instead. See handleNodeInfo: this helper is invoked\n\t// only when remote.Kind == leaf.\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// compareInternal pushes children whose hashes differ.\nfunc (s *session) compareInternal(n *Node, prefix string, local, remote [2]core.ChildInfo) {\n\t// Push in reverse bit order so bit 0 is processed first (LIFO).\n\tfor bit := 1; bit >= 0; bit-- {\n\t\tlc, rc := local[bit], remote[bit]\n\t\tif !lc.Present && !rc.Present {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Both present with equal child digest: whole subtrees agree — prune.\n\t\tif lc.Present && rc.Present && lc.Hash == rc.Hash {\n\t\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.LeafPrunes++ })\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Differ (or one side empty): descend.\n\t\ts.stack = append(s.stack, frame{prefix: prefix + string(rune('0'+bit))})\n\t}\n\ts.afterEqualPrefix(n)\n}\n\n// compareLeaves performs the ordered key merge of two leaf summary lists and\n// enumerates the keys that must be pulled: remote-only keys (missing locally)\n// and keys whose summary differs with the remote version newer. proto.TypeSyncEnd, Session: s.sessionID,\n\t\tInitiator: n.ID, Peer: s.peer, Round: s.round,\n\t\tEnd: &proto.SyncEnd{},\n\t})\n\ts.inFlight = false\n\ts.phase = phaseIdle\n\ts.stack = nil\n\tn.count(func(c *Counters) {\n\t\tc.RoundsCompleted++\n\t\tc.SyncsCompleted++\n\t})\n}\n\n// ensure sim import stays when timeout helpers change.\nvar _ = sim.NewNetwork\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_19dd8b4c2c4de6e7e2cda00a","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1123,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":68408,"output_tokens":4136,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_1hiycywmp2aoq6zl2y7hblov":{"content":"package Equal child hashes prune whole subtrees with zero transfer.\nfunc (s *session) compareInternal(n *Node, prefix string, local, remote [2]core.ChildInfo) {\n\tfor bit := 1; bit >= 0; bit-- {\n\t\tlc, rc := local[bit], remote[bit]\n\t\tif !lc.Present && !rc.Present {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif lc.Present && rc.Present && lc.Hash == rc.Hash {\n\t\t\tn.count(func(c *Counters) { c.LeafPrunes++ })\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\ts.stack = append(s.stack, frame{prefix: prefix + string(rune('0'+bit))})\n\t}\n}\n\n// compareLeaves is the ordered-key-space merge at a leaf. Two versions are totally ordered so that\n// last-writer-wins is deterministic even if the clocks disagree: first compare\n// Seq, then Origin lexicographically.  Deletions are regular writes carrying a\n// tombstone, so the same ordering rules apply.\ntype Version struct {\n\tSeq    int64  `json:\"seq\"`\n\tOrigin string `json:\"origin\"`\n}\n\n// Compare returns -1, 0 or 1: v < w, v == w or v > w.\nfunc (v Version) Compare(w Version) int {\n\tif v.Seq != w.Seq {\n\t\tif v.Seq < w.Seq {\n\t\t\treturn -1\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn 1\n\t}\n\treturn bytes.Compare([]byte(v.Origin), []byte(w.Origin))\n}\n\nfunc (v Version) String() string {\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%d\", v.Origin, v.Seq)\n}\n\n// Entry is one keyspace record. Deleted is a tombstone: the entry is retained\n// (rather than physically removed) so that deletions can be propagated during\n// anti-entropy.\ntype Entry struct {\n\tKey     string  `json:\"key\"`\n\tValue   []byte  `json:\"value,omitempty\"`\n\tVersion Version `json:\"version\"`\n\tDeleted bool    `json:\"deleted\"`\n}\n\n// EncodeSize returns the number of bytes this entry occupies when carried on\n// the wire using the protocol's canonical JSON encoding.\nfunc (e Entry) EncodeSize() int {\n\tb, _ := json.Marshal(wireEntry{\n\t\tKey:     e.Key,\n\t\tValue:   e.Value,\n\t\tVersion: e.Version,\n\t\tDeleted: e.Deleted,\n\t})\n\treturn len(b)\n}\n\n// Store is an ordered in-memory map of entries.  It keeps deleted entries as\n// tombstones; LiveEntry exposes the non-tombstone view used by most callers.\ntype Store struct {\n\tentries map[string]Entry\n\t// counter is the local logical clock of the node owning the store.\n\tcounter int64\n\torigin  string\n\t// mutation counts so Merkle trees can cache aggressively.\n\tversion int64\n}\n\n// NewStore creates a store for node origin.\nfunc NewStore(origin string) *Store {\n\treturn &Store{entries: map[string]Entry{}, origin: origin}\n}\n\n// Origin returns the node id this store belongs to.\nfunc (s *Store) Origin() string { return s.origin }\n\n// MutVersion increments whenever the store changes; used for cache invalidation.\nfunc (s *Store) MutVersion() int64 { return s.version }\n\n// Put applies a write (possibly a delete) stamped with the local logical clock.\nfunc (s *Store) Put(key string, value []byte, deleted bool) Entry {\n\ts.counter++\n\te := Entry{\n\t\tKey:     key,\n\t\tValue:   append([]byte(nil), value...),\n\t\tVersion: Version{Seq: s.counter, Origin: s.origin},\n\t\tDeleted: deleted,\n\t}\n\ts.entries[key] = e\n\ts.version++\n\treturn e\n}\n\n// PutSeeded installs an entry with an explicit version (scenario setup / replay\n// only — normal writes go through Put).\nfunc (s *Store) PutSeeded(e Entry) {\n\tif e.Version.Origin == \"\" {\n\t\te.Version.Origin = s.origin\n\t}\n\tif e.Version.Seq > s.counter {\n\t\ts.counter = e.Version.Seq\n\t}\n\ts.entries[e.Key] = e\n\ts.version++\n}\n\n// Get returns the entry (including tombstones) and presence in the log.\nfunc (s *Store) Get(key string) (Entry, bool) {\n\te, ok := s.entries[key]\n\treturn e, ok\n}\n\n// LiveEntry returns the entry only if it is present and not a tombstone.\nfunc (s *Store) LiveEntry(key string) (Entry, bool) {\n\te, ok := s.entries[key]\n\tif !ok || e.Deleted {\n\t\treturn Entry{}, false\n\t}\n\treturn e, true\n}\n\n// Merge applies a remote entry under last-writer-wins semantics. It returns\n// true if the remote entry was newer and changed the store. Tombstones are\n// merged exactly like ordinary writes, which is how deletions propagate.\nfunc (s *Store) Merge(remote Entry) bool {\n\tcur, ok := s.entries[remote.Key]\n\tif ok && cur.Version.Compare(remote.Version) >= 0 {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif remote.Version.Origin != s.origin && remote.Version.Seq > s.counter {\n\t\ts.counter = remote.Version.Seq\n\t}\n\ts.entries[remote.Key] = cloneEntry(remote)\n\ts.version++\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// AllEntries returns every log entry (tombstones included), key-sorted.\nfunc (s *Store) AllEntries() []Entry {\n\tout := make([]Entry, 0, len(s.entries))\n\tfor _, e := range s.entries {\n\t\tout = append(out, cloneEntry(e))\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Key < out[j].Key })\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// LiveEntries returns all non-tombstone entries, key-sorted.\nfunc (s *Store) LiveEntries() []Entry {\n\tall := s.AllEntries()\n\tout := all[:0:0]\n\tfor _, e := range all {\n\t\tif !e.Deleted {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, e)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// Counts returns live key count, tombstone count and log size.\nfunc (s *Store) Counts() (live, dead, total int) {\n\tfor _, e := range s.entries {\n\t\ttotal++\n\t\tif e.Deleted {\n\t\t\tdead++\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tlive++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn\n}\n\nfunc cloneEntry(e Entry) Entry {\n\tcp := e\n\tcp.Value = append([]byte(nil), e.Value...)\n\treturn cp\n}\n\n// EqualLog reports whether two stores contain exactly the same log entries\n// (values, versions and tombstones). Used for convergence checking.\nfunc EqualLog(a, b *Store) bool {\n\tif len(a.entries) != len(b.entries) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tfor k, ea := range a.entries {\n\t\teb, ok := b.entries[k]\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t\tif ea.Version != eb.Version || ea.Deleted != eb.Deleted ||\n\t\t\t!bytes.Equal(ea.Value, eb.Value) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// wireEntry is the JSON shape used both on the wire and for size accounting.\ntype wireEntry struct {\n\tKey     string  `json:\"key\"`\n\tValue   []byte  `json:\"value,omitempty\"`\n\tVersion Version `json:\"version\"`\n\tDeleted bool    `json:\"deleted\"`\n}\n\n// MarshalEntries / UnmarshalEntries give the protocol one canonical encoding.\nfunc MarshalEntries(entries []Entry) ([]byte, error) {\n\tw := make([]wireEntry, len(entries))\n\tfor i, e := range entries {\n\t\tw[i] = wireEntry{Key: e.Key, Value: e.Value, Version: e.Version, Deleted: e.Deleted}\n\t}\n\treturn json.Marshal(w)\n}\n\n// UnmarshalEntries parses the canonical encoding.\nfunc UnmarshalEntries(data []byte) ([]Entry, error) {\n\tvar w []wireEntry\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(data, &w);
